description: Phase 9 Track A: production hardening per AUDIT.md (repo root — read it first; work follows its 'Recommended remediation order'). Six areas: (1) authn/authz/tenant isolation/safe errors, (2) atomic idempotent lifecycle execution, (3) post-settlement compensation saga, (4) fixed-precision monetary model, (5) key custody and approval minimization, (6) audit anchoring + defensive web controls + scalability. Constraints: never break the local demo flow (npm run setup && npm run dev must keep working end to end), keep all AGENTS.md invariants (state machine, append-only hash-chained audit, money types, per-network accounts, compliance fail-safe), and extend the vitest suite with every story.

userStories.title: API-key identity model: ApiKey table, lib/auth.ts, seeded dev keys
userStories.description: As an operator, I want every API caller to have an authenticated identity so that no route is anonymous. Foundation only — enforcement comes in US-003/US-004.
acceptanceCriteria: Prisma model ApiKey: id, keyHash (sha256 hex of the raw key), role enum string ('OPERATOR' | 'REVIEWER' | 'ENTITY'), entityId nullable FK (required when role=ENTITY), label, createdAt
lib/auth.ts: authenticate(request) reads x-api-key header, falls back to sos_key cookie; returns Principal { role, entityId?, label } or null; sha256 lookup, no plaintext keys stored

scripts/setup.mjs seeds keys: one OPERATOR, one REVIEWER, one ENTITY key per seeded entity; prints raw keys to console and writes them to gitignored chain/dev-api-keys.json (add to .gitignore if the existing patterns don't already cover it)
tests/helpers fixture seeds the same key set and exposes raw keys to tests
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Login page + principal cookie so the demo UI keeps working
userStories.description: As a demo user, I want to sign in with an API key and have the UI act as that principal so that enforcement (next stories) doesn't break the browser flow.
acceptanceCriteria: /login page: paste an API key, POST to /api/auth/login which validates it and sets an httpOnly sos_key cookie; invalid key shows a generic error
/api/auth/logout clears the cookie
App shell (sidebar) shows the signed-in principal's label + role and a sign-out link; shows a sign-in link when anonymous
Server components can resolve the current principal from cookies() (document the pattern in scripts/ralph/CLAUDE.md if non-obvious)
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Enforce authz + tenant scoping on all read routes
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want reads scoped to the caller so that one tenant cannot see another tenant's data.
acceptanceCriteria: Unauthenticated request to any API route returns 401 with a generic JSON error
GET /api/payments and /api/payments/[id]: OPERATOR and REVIEWER see all; ENTITY sees only payments where it is sender or recipient (404 on others' payment ids, not 403, to avoid existence leaks)
GET /api/entities: OPERATOR/REVIEWER see all; ENTITY sees only itself
GET /api/balances, /api/reconciliation, /api/audit: OPERATOR and REVIEWER only
GET /api/networks stays public (static registry data, no tenant data)
Integration tests cover: 401 anonymous, ENTITY cross-tenant 404, ENTITY own-payment 200, REVIEWER read-all 200
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Enforce authz on write routes; audit actor from authenticated principal
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want writes authorized by role and the audit trail to record who actually acted, not what the request body claims.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/payments: OPERATOR, or ENTITY whose entityId matches sender_id; quote/execute/cancel: OPERATOR or the payment's sender entity
POST /api/payments/[id]/review: REVIEWER (or OPERATOR) only; the reviewer identity comes from the principal — remove any reviewer/actor field from the request body
Treasury routes (park/recall/accrue): OPERATOR only; positions GET: OPERATOR/REVIEWER
audit() actor is the authenticated principal's label/role everywhere a route triggers an audit event (grep for audit( call sites in app/api)
Integration tests: ENTITY cannot review, ENTITY cannot create a payment with another sender_id, REVIEWER decision audits the reviewer principal as actor
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Safe error handling: generic client errors, details server-side only
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want API errors to stop leaking internals (the execute route currently returns raw error messages, including RPC/contract detail).
acceptanceCriteria: lib/api-errors.ts: one helper mapping thrown errors to { error_code, message } with stable codes (unauthorized, forbidden, not_found, invalid_request, conflict, execution_failed, internal); full error logged via console.error on the server only
All app/api route handlers use the helper for their catch paths; execute route no longer returns raw err.message or stack
Payment.failureReason in API responses is replaced by a safe summary for ENTITY callers; OPERATOR/REVIEWER still see the stored detail
Integration test: forced execute failure returns execution_failed with no contract address / RPC URL / stack in the body
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Compare-and-swap status transitions
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want every lifecycle transition to be conditional on the expected current status so that concurrent writers cannot corrupt state.
acceptanceCriteria: Executor setStatus (and any raw prisma.payment.update that changes status) becomes updateMany({ where: { id, status: expectedFrom }, data }) — zero rows updated throws a typed StaleTransitionError; assertTransition still runs first
The review and cancel routes use the same CAS path
DB test: two simulated concurrent transitions from the same status — exactly one wins, the loser gets StaleTransitionError and the payment ends in a single consistent status
Audit event is only written when the CAS update succeeded
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Per-payment execution lease claimed atomically with liquidity reservation
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want double-execution to be impossible: one lease per payment, claimed in the same DB transaction that reserves liquidity.
acceptanceCriteria: Payment gets executionLeaseId + leasedAt columns; execute claims the lease with a CAS update (WHERE id = ? AND executionLeaseId IS NULL AND status = 'APPROVED') inside the same prisma.$transaction that creates the LiquidityReservation
Second concurrent execute returns 409 conflict (error_code conflict) without touching chain state
Lease is cleared on terminal states (SETTLED/FAILED/REFUNDED/COMPENSATED) so operator retries stay possible where the state machine allows
Integration test: fire two executes concurrently at one APPROVED payment on the local fixture chains — exactly one settles, the other 409s, exactly one escrow tx exists on-chain
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Idempotency keys for write endpoints
userStories.description: As an API consumer, I want to retry a write safely so that network retries cannot double-create or double-execute.
acceptanceCriteria: IdempotencyRecord prisma model: key (unique per principal), route, requestHash, responseStatus, responseBody, createdAt
POST /api/payments and POST /api/payments/[id]/execute honor an Idempotency-Key header: same key + same request body replays the stored response; same key + different body returns 422
Records expire after 24h (checked at read time — no cron needed)
Integration tests: duplicate create with same key returns the same payment_id and creates one row; conflicting body 422s
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Compensation saga for destination-leg failure after source settlement
userStories.description: As a sender, I want my funds compensated if the payout leg fails after escrow was already released to treasury, instead of the payment just being marked FAILED.
acceptanceCriteria: New lifecycle statuses in lib/state.ts: COMPENSATION_PENDING (reachable from PAYOUT_PENDING) and COMPENSATED (terminal, from COMPENSATION_PENDING), enforced by assertTransition; state-machine unit tests updated

Executor: if the destination payout or ledger-credit step throws AFTER settlePayment succeeded, do NOT call failAndRefund (escrow is already released); instead transition to COMPENSATION_PENDING, send a treasury-funded transfer of the source asset amount back to the sender wallet on the source network, then transition to COMPENSATED
Every compensation step audited (tx hashes as strings, never bigint, in audit detail — AGENTS.md gotcha)

Liquidity reservation released; integration test forces a destination failure after settlement (injectable test-only failure hook in the executor) and asserts the sender's source-asset balance is restored
Reconcile on-chain facts before compensating: read the escrow contract's payment status to confirm SETTLED on-chain rather than trusting the DB alone
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Operator repair view for partial settlements
userStories.description: As an operator, I want to see payments stuck in partial states and retry/compensate them so that no payment is silently stranded.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/payments?stuck=true (OPERATOR only) lists payments in COMPENSATION_PENDING or FAILED-with-escrow states, including the on-chain escrow status read live from the source network (degrade gracefully if RPC is down, per AGENTS.md)
POST /api/payments/[id]/repair (OPERATOR only) retries the compensation path for COMPENSATION_PENDING payments, idempotently
Dashboard shows a 'needs attention' count linking to a simple list of stuck payments
Integration test: a payment forced into COMPENSATION_PENDING is repaired to COMPENSATED via the endpoint
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Strict canonical decimal validation at the API boundary
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want malformed or over-precise amounts rejected so that '1e6', 'Infinity', and 25000.001 JPY can never enter the system.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/money.ts: parseAmount(amountStr, currency) accepting only ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ with at most the currency's decimal places (JPY 0, USD/SGD 2), no leading '+', no exponent, max 15 integer digits; returns bigint minor units; throws typed MoneyError otherwise — excess precision is REJECTED, never truncated
POST /api/payments validates amount via parseAmount and stores the canonical string form; invalid input returns 400 invalid_request with a safe message
Unit tests: scientific notation, Infinity, NaN, negative, empty, '25000.001' JPY rejected; '25000.00' USD, '0.01' USD, '100' JPY accepted with correct minor units
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: FX and fee math on bigint minor units
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want quoting/fee arithmetic off JS floats so that every quoted figure is exact.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/fx.ts computes spread, slippage, platform fee, and destination amount in bigint minor units (basis-point math with explicit floor rounding), converting to display strings only at the edge
Quote API responses are unchanged in shape (strings); update test fixtures where floor-rounding legitimately shifts the last minor unit and call it out in notes
No Number() arithmetic on monetary values remains in lib/fx.ts (Number allowed only for bps constants and display formatting)
Unit tests: known-rate fixtures assert exact bigint results incl. JPY 0-decimals and a value that would lose precision as a float (> 2^53 minor units)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Liquidity and routing math on bigint
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want liquidity checks exact so that reservation accounting can never drift from float rounding.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/routing.ts availableLiquidity/liquidityOk and reservation sums use bigint end to end (reserved amounts parsed from DB strings via lib/money.ts)
Executor liquidity reservation + treasury.freeTreasuryBalance callers agree on bigint units (treasury.ts is already bigint — do not regress it)
Import direction preserved: routing → treasury only (AGENTS.md gotcha)
Unit test: liquidity boundary exact-equal passes, one minor unit over fails (both directions)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Exact per-payment allowances instead of unlimited approvals
userStories.description: As a security owner, I want entity wallets to grant only the allowance each escrow needs so that a compromised contract cannot drain wallets.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/setup.mjs and scripts/deploy-testnet.mjs stop granting MAX allowance from entity wallets

Executor ensures an exact allowance before initiatePayment: read current allowance; if insufficient, entity wallet approves exactly the escrow amount; the escrow call that depends on the approval tx uses retryOnReplicaLag (lib/chain.ts)
Existing deployed testnets keep working: allowance >= needed short-circuits (already-granted MAX allowances are fine)
Integration test: fresh entity wallet with zero prior allowance settles a payment; allowance after settlement is 0 (fully consumed)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Signer abstraction + server-only chain modules
userStories.description: As a security owner, I want signing behind one interface and chain/key code impossible to bundle client-side, so custody can later move to a KMS without touching callers.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/signers.ts: Signer interface (address + viem account construction) with LocalKeySigner implementation; lib/chain.ts wallet construction goes through it; a KmsSigner stub documents the extension point (throws 'not configured')
import 'server-only' added to lib/chain.ts, lib/signers.ts, lib/treasury.ts, lib/executor.ts; app builds (npm run build) — lib/networks.ts must stay client-safe
Deployment credentials separated from runtime: deploy scripts read DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY directly; runtime operator writes resolve via the signer layer; document the boundary in AGENTS.md
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Atomic domain-change + audit-event writes
userStories.description: As an auditor, I want every audit event committed in the same transaction as the change it describes so the log can never disagree with state.
acceptanceCriteria: audit() accepts an optional Prisma transaction client; all status-changing paths (executor setStatus CAS, review, cancel, treasury park/recall/accrue) write domain change + audit event in one prisma.$transaction
Hash-chain serialization is preserved (the findFirst-for-prevHash and create stay inside the same tx; document the serialization guarantee in a comment)
DB test: a transaction forced to fail after the domain write leaves NO audit event and NO domain change (both roll back together)
Audit chain verifier still reports INTACT over the full suite run
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Signed audit checkpoints + incremental verification
userStories.description: As an auditor, I want periodically signed chain roots so tampering is detectable even by someone with DB write access, and verification stays fast as the log grows.
acceptanceCriteria: AuditCheckpoint prisma model: id, lastEventId, chainHash, signature (HMAC-SHA256 over chainHash with AUDIT_ANCHOR_KEY from .env), createdAt; checkpoint written automatically every 100 events (configurable) and on demand via POST /api/audit/checkpoint (OPERATOR only)
GET /api/audit verifies incrementally: validate the latest checkpoint signature, then re-hash only events after it; response includes checkpoint coverage info
Tamper test: modifying an event before a signed checkpoint is detected via signature mismatch even if the attacker re-hashes the whole chain (they lack AUDIT_ANCHOR_KEY)
Missing AUDIT_ANCHOR_KEY degrades gracefully to full-chain verification with a warning flag in the response (demo stays functional)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Security headers, rate limits, pagination, bounded exports
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want baseline web hardening so the app is safe to put behind a real URL.
acceptanceCriteria: next.config.ts sets security headers on all routes: Content-Security-Policy (self + inline styles as Tailwind requires), X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options DENY, Permissions-Policy
Simple in-memory rate limiter keyed by principal (fallback: IP) on write endpoints: 429 with Retry-After beyond 30 writes/min; JSON body size capped at 64KB with 413 beyond

GET /api/payments and GET /api/audit paginated (limit default 50 max 200, cursor param); UI list pages pass paging params; reconciliation CSV bounded to a date range (query params, default last 30 days) and writes one summary audit event per export instead of auditing every download row (AUDIT.md rationale)
Integration tests: 429 after burst, 413 oversize body, pagination cursor walks the full set exactly once
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
